companions.name: Spica B
companions.description: The smaller star of Spica, 3.7 times the Sun's width, orbiting its partner every four days.

radius.source: Tkachenko et al. (2016), MNRAS 458, 1964, Table 7: secondary radius 3.74 +/- 0.53 solar radii

mass.source: Tkachenko et al. (2016), MNRAS 458, 1964, Table 7: dynamical mass of the secondary 7.21 +/- 0.75 solar masses

temperature.source: Tkachenko et al. (2016), MNRAS 458, 1964, Tables 4 and 7: secondary Teff 20,900 +/- 800 K from the disentangled spectrum

orbit.source: Tkachenko et al. (2016), MNRAS 458, 1964, Table 2 (PHOEBE 2.0 solution): P 4.0145 d, T0 HJD 2,454,189.40 the time of periastron passage (Sect. 3; MJD 54188.90, HJD for BJD_TDB), e 0.133, longitude of periastron 255.6 degrees (the primary's, from its radial velocities), i 63.1; a 28.20 solar radii over the primary's 7.47 is 3.775 of its radii. The node's position angle on the sky is not measured and is drawn at 0, a display convention

text.card: The smaller star of Spica, 3.7 times the Sun's width, orbiting its partner every four days.
text.introduction: Its orbit weighs it at 7.21 solar masses; it is 3.74 solar radii with 20,900 K at its surface.
